text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bosnia's Council of Ministers agrees the final version of its working regulations, granting voting rights only to the council co-chairmen, deputy co-chairman and ministers.

- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation President and member of the country's collective presidency Kresimir Zubak admits that Croat police were involved in the incident in Mostar on Monday when one Moslem was killed and 22 wounded. He blames Moslem deputy mayor Safet Orucevic for leading procession of Moslems who were attacked.

- Minister of Interior of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation Mehmed Zilic and his Bosnian Serb counterpart Dragan Kijac agree measures to enhance safety of citizens from both entities in the period following the announcement of the arbitration decision over disputed north Bosnian town of Brcko.

- Events in Mostar might have an impact on the arbitration decision over disputed Bosnian town of Brcko because Bosnian Serb representatives have, during the arbitration process in Rome, cited Mostar as an example where common life is imposible, Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation President Kresimir Zubak tells news conference.
- Arbitration over disputed Bosnian town of Brcko will decide to place the town under a temporary international protectorate, Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation Minister of justice Mato Tadic says.
